steps.path: When the assistant wants to run an admin command (Ask first or Auto-edit mode)
steps.headline: Every mode now shows the same admin stop you approved for Full auto, with nothing under the buttons.
steps.changed: Your R-1 note: the Ask-first card is now the Full auto band, command included. Only the grey line differs: 'This always asks', since 'Full auto still stops here' would be false outside Full auto.
steps.notice: One look for an admin command in every mode: Run it / Skip it, never Always Allow.

steps.path: Right after you press Run it on an admin command
steps.headline: The password box is full width with a show/hide eye inside it, and one Confirm button below.
steps.changed: Your R-3 note: the field spans the card, the eye on its right shows or hides what you typed, and Run it / Skip it became one full-width Confirm.
steps.notice: Confirm stays dim until you type something. The eye resets to hidden after a wrong try.
steps.risk: With no Skip, backing out here means the chat's Stop button, which stops the whole command.

steps.headline: A wrong password now shows a yellow warning banner above the box.
steps.changed: Your R-4 note: the same yellow warning box the app uses elsewhere, titled 'Wrong password', with the tries left inside.
steps.notice: Hard to miss; the box is emptied for the next try.

steps.headline: The last-try lockout warning sits in the same yellow banner.
steps.changed: Your R-5 note: the lockout sentence moved into the banner.
steps.notice: You're warned before a lockout, in the one place you're already looking.

highlight.text: 1 try left. Another wrong one may lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes.

steps.path: A command you approved asks for admin partway through (an install script)
steps.headline: A script asking partway through now gets a highlighted box naming the script, instead of a long sentence.
steps.changed: Your R-6 note: 'Asked partway through install.sh' is a boxed title, with 'Only type your password if you expected this step' under it. The rest matches the normal password card.
steps.notice: The unusual case looks unusual at a glance.
